summary: Ten HN comment recommendations, from browser-based booklet printing to local garage controls and a rugged Raspberry Pi build.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 stories processed; 7,330 comments | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Bookbinder JS
items.source_story_title: Making 8-page foldable zines from a single A4 sheet in the browser
items.summary: Browser tool that rearranges PDF pages for printing foldable zines and booklets.
items.why_included: A recurring use case for home printing makes this more than a folding demo.
items.evidence: A commenter uses it regularly to print booklets for their kids and confirms it handles the single-sheet zine fold.

evidence_sources.author: drunkboxer
evidence_sources.excerpt: Bookbinder js is the best. I use it to print multi-page booklets for my kids often. It does cover this exact folding algorithm as well.

items.name: Open Source Ecology
items.source_story_title: Everything you need to survive and rebuild society
items.summary: Open blueprints for building industrial machines and homes yourself.
items.why_included: It takes open design beyond desktop projects and into community infrastructure.
items.evidence: A commenter praised the project's ambition, pointing to homes and bulldozers as examples of the scale involved.

evidence_sources.author: jmathai
evidence_sources.excerpt: A related project is Open Source Ecology (terrible name), which aims to make the tools necessary to rebuild society accessible to everyone. Think houses and bulldozers, not hammers...impressive stuff.

items.name: Rector
items.summary: Automated PHP upgrades and refactoring; still review the changes before merging.
items.why_included: Two independent reports give concrete examples of the legacy PHP upgrades it can help with.
items.evidence: Commenters credited Rector with helping them move from PHP 7.4 to 8.3 and 8.4; one still needed manual fixes and reported one breakage.

evidence_sources.author: nticompass
evidence_sources.excerpt: Rector is great! It's what I used to help migrate from PHP 7.4 to 8.3. I did still have to manually fix things and there was one spot where Rector broke the code, but I don't know what I'd've done without it.

evidence_sources.author: asimovDev
evidence_sources.excerpt: Don't forget to use Rector[0] if you haven't already. Helped me tremendously when going 7.4 > 8.4

items.name: Ragel
items.source_story_title: Multiple vulnerabilities in Regexp and String case conversion
items.summary: State-machine compiler that turns regular expressions into embeddable parser code.
items.why_included: It's a practical option when a parser needs named actions rather than just matching text.
items.evidence: In a discussion of compiling regex-driven parsers into embeddable code, a commenter said they had used Ragel extensively and liked it.

evidence_sources.author: wiml
evidence_sources.excerpt: In the past I've used Ragel extensively for this kind of thing - really a nice tool in the same space.

evidence_sources.author: Spivak
evidence_sources.excerpt: What you're describing is using a parser generator to take a regex and turn it into code you can embed into your project.

items.name: zswap
items.summary: Linux kernel feature that caches compressed swap pages in RAM to reduce disk I/O.
items.why_included: It's a built-in Linux tuning option backed by a recommendation from someone running it on several systems.
items.evidence: A commenter who uses zswap on most of their systems said they generally find it beneficial.

evidence_sources.author: rustyhancock
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've used zswap on most of my systems and generally find it beneficial especially as (de)compression can be very fast these days.

items.name: HCPBridgeMqtt
items.source_story_title: Dumping an AES key from a MyQ garage opener to stop rebooting when offline
items.summary: ESP32 bridge for controlling compatible Hörmann garage doors locally over MQTT.
items.why_included: The recommendation comes from sustained use, not a quick bench test.
items.evidence: A commenter reported about a year of reliable use with their setup.

evidence_sources.author: blutack
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use this one: https://github.com/Gifford47/HCPBridgeMqtt and it's been rock solid for about a year now.

items.name: Konnected
items.summary: Garage-door retrofit controllers that integrate with Home Assistant and can bridge into Apple Home.
items.why_included: A first-hand report confirms the Home Assistant-to-Apple Home path on one opener.
items.evidence: A commenter used Konnected with a Chamberlain opener and said it worked well with Home Assistant and Apple Home bridging.

evidence_sources.author: philips
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have used https://konnected.io with my newish Chamberlin. It works great with HomeAssistant and bridging it into Apple Home.

items.name: Raspberry Pi Recovery Kit
items.source_story_title: Everything you need to survive and rebuild society
items.summary: Jay Doscher’s DIY rugged Raspberry Pi computer for keeping references accessible offline.
items.why_included: It's a documented build with a parts list for a tangible offline-computing project.
items.evidence: A commenter praised Doscher’s portable Pi build and pointed readers back to its original 2019 appearance on HN.

evidence_sources.author: pugworthy
evidence_sources.excerpt: Jay Doscher has been building and evolving his Recovery Kit for a while. It's a portable RPi loaded with lots of useful content to load on it. Pretty neat build. First shared here in 2019...

items.name: Lord of the io_uring
items.source_story_title: 15M web servers on one VM – smoltcp, DPDK, AF_XDP
items.summary: Guide to asynchronous Linux I/O, from epoll fundamentals to services built with io_uring.
items.why_included: It teaches the earlier I/O model before introducing the newer interface.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended the series for its walkthrough from epoll and kqueue to asynchronous services with io_uring.

evidence_sources.author: gavinray
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you enjoyed this post, you might also like the "Lord of the io_uring" series which walks through how epoll/kqueue work and then onto async services with io_uring:

items.name: Does Advertising Actually Work? (Part 2: Digital)
items.source_story_title: The 98% Slot Machine: How Paid Advertising Became an Extraction Tax
items.summary: Freakonomics Radio episode on measuring online ads and who benefits from overstating their impact.
items.why_included: It brings measurement and incentives into a conversation often dominated by ad-platform metrics.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended the episode and highlighted its discussion of ad sellers’ incentive to oversell effectiveness.

evidence_sources.author: hackthemack
evidence_sources.excerpt: It is worth checking out. Here is a relevant couple of quotes... HWANG: I think a second thing is, a little bit like in the subprime-mortgage crisis, you do have people who have very perverse incentives, I think, to push the effectiveness of online ads. That’s the ad agencies, the ad platforms themselves, the people who run ad technology.
